title: [roles.implement] args = ["--approve"] is dead config after the herdr re-cut
body:
The args are pi-CLI trust flags that the HERDR executor compiles into an implement agent's argv — but after tick 2q5 the herdr profile set routes implement onto the local-subprocess executor, which never reads roles-table args, and the durable Node host takes no --approve flag. On every substrate the pairing now does nothing, while its comment still explains pi's trust model as if it launched. A reader of runners.toml will believe implement workers somewhere run with --approve. Cleanup (drop the args, reword the comment) belongs to the operator's routing file; jhp's sweep of the pi-CLI remnants is a natural moment.
evidence: .tick/runners.toml [roles.implement] args = ["--approve"] beside kind = "pi"; internal/cli/executor.go spawnArgv is the only consumer, reached only for herdr dispatches
